name: Laya v0.4 Decision Engine API (Jev-Compatible)
description: Self-hosted Laya API: typed choice, score and yes/no decisions on CPU.

upstream.package: laya 0.4.28 from PyPI, wheel sha256 ad54941b65da960e6893f72e2d96d894bf03a9d33e1305dbfb97b57d54d0b3e6 (same digest as the GitHub release asset)

LAYA_API_KEY.description: Bearer key for every API call (Authorization: Bearer {key}). Generated at deploy; the server will not start without one of 24+ characters.

PORT.description: Port laya-serve listens on (all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses). The healthcheck and the public domain use it; leave as is.

LAYA_MODELS.description: Checkpoints loaded at startup: english, multilingual, typed-decisions. Default: the two automatic routing picks between (about 3.7 GB RAM).

LAYA_DEFAULT_MODEL.description: Checkpoint for text whose language can't be detected. Empty = multilingual (upstream default); set english for mostly-English traffic.

LAYA_MAX_LOADED.description: Checkpoints kept in memory at once (empty = upstream default 2). 1 caps RAM but reloads a checkpoint on every switch.

LAYA_REVISION.description: Hugging Face revision for checkpoint downloads. 'reviewed' = the commit laya 0.4.28 pins. Clear it to follow the Hub's latest.

TEMPLATE_VERIFY_DIGESTS.description: Check each checkpoint's files against SHA-256 digests recorded for the reviewed revision before loading (only with LAYA_REVISION=reviewed).

TEMPLATE_VEGA_LANE.description: off: states past ~8k tokens stay on the encoders and are truncated. auto: laya's vega lane reads them with a 0.8B reader (+2-4 GB RAM, slow on CPU).

LAYA_THREADS.description: Torch CPU threads. Empty = the service's CPU quota, at most 8 (more threads than CPU time stalls inference).

LAYA_JEV_STRICT.description: 1 = strict Jev wire format (no routing, action or extra confidence fields) for clients that reject unknown fields.

LAYA_LOG_LEVEL.description: Server log level: critical, error, warning, info, debug or trace.

HF_TOKEN.description: Optional Hugging Face token. The checkpoints are public; a token only helps against Hub download rate limits.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Seconds a stopping deployment gets to finish in-flight requests on redeploy.
